financing.summary: Home Creations is a private, family-owned, conventional for-sale builder with no public debt, no SEC filings and no published lender, credit facility, land banker or capital partner. What is public points to a self-funded, owner-developer model in Oklahoma: land development is an in-house function, co-founder Jalal Farzaneh is reported as owner of Shaz Investments (a Norman land developer), and an engineering firm says Home Creations hired it to plan a 760-acre, roughly 2,000-unit community in Norman. In Houston, entered in 2022, its lot sources are not disclosed: the company names no developer for its Houston communities. A 2015 profile quoted a company executive saying the owners reinvest most earnings and that a shortage of developed lots was the main brake on growth. It is a plausible land-banking customer on two fronts (the large Norman tract and Houston lot supply), but there is no public sign that the family has used outside land capital.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, with no stated owned-versus-optioned target. In Oklahoma the family entitles and develops much of its own land through affiliates and an in-house land development department, then builds it out. In Houston the lot source (own development or third-party developers) is not disclosed.

lots.note: No lot counts are published. For scale only: on 2026-11-19 the company site showed 21 locations and 209 available homes in the Oklahoma City market and 8 locations and 39 available homes in Houston. These are homes for sale, not lots.

land_banking.description: Land development company whose owner is reported to be Home Creations co-founder Jalal Farzaneh. In October 2021 Norman's city council voted 7-2 against its request to build 147 homes in southeast Norman next to Eagle Cliff South; its attorney said the council had approved similar Shaz requests two years earlier. Home Creations lists Eagle Cliff in Norman as a current community.
land_banking.source_title: Norman Transcript via Yahoo: Council mostly quiet on reasons for 'no' votes for requested development
land_banking.note: This is family self-development, not third-party land banking. The report is from 2021; the outcome of the 147-home request (any lawsuit or re-filing) and the affiliate's current activity were not checked. The lot figure is the number of homes in the rejected request.

land_banking.description: Engineering firm HR Green says Home Creations chose it for a 760-acre mixed-use community in Norman with single-family and multi-family homes, commercial space, more than 233 acres of open space and about 2,000 units. The owning entity, timing and funding are not stated.
land_banking.source_title: HR Green project page: Norman Residential Development
land_banking.note: The page is undated (site footer shows 2025) and gives no project name, so entitlement status is unknown. About 2,000 units is the consultant's total for all housing types, not a single-family lot count. This is the largest visible land-capital need in the company's pipeline.

gaps: Houston lot sources: verification 2026-11-19 removed a 'third-party developers in Houston' row; its cited post (Inside Grand Oaks Reserve, 2026-07-17) names no developer or other builders and says Home Creations plans the community's build-out, so whether Houston lots are bought or self-developed is not public.
Lots owned and optioned, years of supply: not publicly disclosed (private company).

Construction lenders, land loans, credit facility terms: not publicly disclosed. County mortgage records, which would name the banks, could not be read (the Oklahoma county records site blocks automated access).
Land banker, lot-option partner or outside capital partner: none found in any source opened.

Links to Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon: none found, but the dedicated search was not run because the swarm's shared web-search allowance ran out partway through this run.

M&A in 2025-2026: none found in the sources opened; a dedicated search was not run for the same reason. The 2022 Houston entry is described by the company as an expansion, with no acquisition mentioned.

Houston lot sources: developer names and lot-purchase terms for Grand Oaks Reserve, Santa Fe, Encino Estates, The Enclave at Spring Branch, Hill & Dale Ranch, Lexington Heights, Spring Ridge and Bentwater are not disclosed by the company.
760-acre Norman project: name, owning entity, entitlement status and funding not stated by the one source (an engineering consultant's undated project page).
Shaz Investments: outcome of the 2021 Norman request and current holdings not checked; other family land entities, if any, not identified.
Balance sheet (debt, cash, leverage): not publicly disclosed. A January 2015 magazine profile quoted a company executive saying the owners reinvest most earnings; nothing newer.
SEC EDGAR: company lookup was blocked during this run; no SEC filer is expected for this private company.
Buyer-mortgage lenders named on the company blog (2021) are retail lenders for homebuyers, not the builder's own lenders, and are left out.
